result: IPD meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=1298) found CBT reduced self-reported fatigue (CIS beta -11.46, 95% CI -15.13 to -7.79), with larger effects in younger, less impaired, fluctuating-activity patients and no moderation by PEM or case definition.
reason: Same intervention and self-report outcomes as the PACE finding; adds moderator and PEM analysis but no objective outcomes, so extends rather than replicates.

result: Interim report: 7 of the first 10 post-COVID ME/CFS patients with raised beta2-AR antibodies responded (SF-36 PF +10 to +35) at week 4 after repeat immunoadsorption.
reason: Already cited: interim report of the same open-label cohort (NCT05629988) published in full as Stein 2024, so not independent.

result: Interim report: 7 of the first 10 post-COVID ME/CFS patients with raised beta2-AR antibodies responded (SF-36 PF +10 to +35) at week 4 after repeat immunoadsorption.
reason: Already cited: interim of the Stein open-label cohort (NCT05629988) in finding_studies; uncontrolled, adds nothing.

result: In 103 post-COVID patients vs 90 healthy controls (and 103 CAD patients), 24-h Holter showed higher LF/HF ratio (p<=0.001), sympathetic predominance and impaired nocturnal parasympathetic activity, worse in those hospitalised acutely.
reason: Same measure and direction (higher LF/HF, reduced vagal tone) but in long COVID, so extends rather than replicates.

result: In 103 post-COVID patients vs 90 healthy controls, 24-h Holter showed higher LF/HF ratio (p<=0.001) and disturbed diurnal HRV with impaired night-time parasympathetic activity.
reason: Finding is about orthostatic testing and MSNA, which the paper did not measure; its HRV and nocturnal parasympathetic result fits the HRV findings.

result: In Taiwanese claims data (395,811 infected cases with 1:1 propensity-matched controls), infection with common pathogens raised CFS risk (aHR 1.5, 95% CI 1.47-1.54), with associations for bacteria, viruses and fungi (including influenza and candida).
reason: Same registry-style exposure measure, but it finds bacterial and fungal as well as viral associations, against the viral-only specificity; may be the preprint of a cited Taiwanese study (Hsu 2024 or Chang 2025), so check before adding.

result: In 18 female ME/CFS patients vs 17 sedentary controls, EV proteomes changed differently after maximal CPET (pre, 15 min, 24 h), and the changes correlated with symptom severity.
reason: Already cited: preprint of Giloteaux 2024 (same design and cohort).

result: In 18 female ME/CFS patients vs 17 sedentary controls, EV proteomes changed differently after maximal CPET, and the changes correlated with symptom severity.
reason: Same Giloteaux dataset already in the finding's re-analysis; it tests the exercise response, not resting EV counts or replicated protein differences.

result: In the first 17,074 DecodeME participants, 83.5% were female; females had more comorbidities, and female sex, older age and illness duration over 10 years were associated with greater severity.
reason: Same DecodeME cohort the finding already cites, so not an independent replication; adds sex differences in comorbidity and severity.

result: DecodeME questionnaire analysis (17,074 participants): sex, age and duration over 10 years were associated with severity, onset types differed in symptoms, and unknown infection status at onset was associated with fibromyalgia.
reason: No genetic data; the sex finding is covered by the endocrine-female-preponderance link and no other finding covers the onset-type and severity results.
